answer_text:
# 🏥 Medi-Cal — What You Need to Know (2026 Updates)

**Medi-Cal** is California's Medicaid program, providing free or low-cost health coverage to eligible low-income individuals and families. Here is a comprehensive overview of the current landscape and major changes:

---

## 📋 What Medi-Cal Covers

Covered benefits include seeing your doctor and going to the hospital or getting emergency care. Medi-Cal members can also fill their prescriptions, get mental health supports, and receive treatment for substance use. Other services covered include regular checkups, shots or vaccines, long-term care, non-emergency medical transportation, dental and vision care.

---

## 🔄 Key Changes: 2026–2028

### 1. 🧾 Asset Limits Reinstated (January 1, 2026)
Effective January 1, 2026, the asset limit has been reinstated for non-MAGI Medi-Cal programs, back to 2022 levels — **$130,000 for an individual**, and **$65,000 for each additional household member**.

Current Medi-Cal beneficiaries will need to provide information about their assets during their next annual renewal that occurs after January 1, 2026.

### 2. 🚫 Enrollment Freeze for Undocumented Adults (January 1, 2026)
Beginning January 1, 2026, new Medi-Cal applications for adults – ages 19 and up – who are undocumented can only qualify for **Emergency Medi-Cal** or **pregnancy-related Medi-Cal**.

However, if you already have Medi-Cal or applied before January 1, 2026, you are eligible to keep your full-scope Medi-Cal coverage, provided you still meet all other eligibility requirements.

### 3. 🦷 Dental Coverage Changes (July 1, 2026)
Starting July 1, 2026, some Medi-Cal members will stop getting full-scope dental services as part of their Medi-Cal coverage. Dental benefits will not be covered for Medi-Cal members ages 19 and up who are undocumented or who do not have satisfactory immigration status.

### 4. 🌐 Immigration Status Reclassification (October 1, 2026)
Starting October 1, 2026, the federal government will change how it classifies some immigration statuses. This may affect eligibility for full-scope Medi-Cal for certain groups such as refugees and asylees.

### 5. 📅 Six-Month Renewals (January 1, 2027)
Effective January 1, 2027, adults ages 19–64 will need to renew Medi-Cal **every six months** instead of annually. Missing deadlines could result in loss of coverage.

### 6. 💼 Work Requirements (January 1, 2027)
Starting January 1, 2027, some adults will need to work, volunteer, or go to school to keep Medi-Cal. If this applies to you, the county Medi-Cal office will send you a letter.

### 7. 💵 Copayments Begin (October 1, 2028)
Beginning October 1, 2028, some adults on Medi-Cal will pay small copayments for certain services, capped at **5 percent of household income**, with **no copays** for emergency care, checkups, pregnancy, pediatric, mental health, or community clinic services.

---

## ✅ What You Should Do Now

- Keep your address and contact information current, and review and respond to all mail from the county.
- Watch your mail and respond quickly to Medi-Cal renewal packets or letters from your health plan or local county Medi-Cal office. Know your renewal date so you can renew your Medi-Cal online or work with your local county Medi-Cal office.
- If you are at risk of losing dental coverage, try to get needed dental care before July 1, 2026. Schedule your cleanings, exams, and any urgent dental work now.

---

## ℹ️ Good News for Most Members

The federal government has made changes that will affect eligibility and benefits; however, **most Medi-Cal members won't see any changes**.

---
